T-001.threat: Data tampering via unauthenticated fieldbus protocol between {{sourceName}} and {{targetName}}
T-001.cause: {{dataFlowName}} carries no integrity protection — data can be modified in transit without detection
T-001.attack: Attacker intercepts and modifies fieldbus frames between {{sourceName}} and {{targetName}} to inject false setpoints

T-002.threat: Data tampering on embedded bus {{dataFlowName}} between {{sourceName}} and {{targetName}}
T-002.cause: Embedded bus carries no integrity protection or authentication — data is transmitted in plaintext
T-002.attack: Attacker attaches a hardware probe to the embedded bus and injects or modifies data packets

T-003.cause: Debug or programming interface is accessible and not locked — attacker can overwrite flash memory directly
T-003.attack: Attacker connects a debug probe to the {{dataFlowName}} interface and overwrites firmware with a malicious image

T-004.threat: Malformed protocol frame injection: Attacker sends crafted frames to corrupt or crash {{targetName}}
T-004.cause: {{targetName}} processes all incoming frames without strict protocol conformance validation
T-004.attack: Attacker crafts protocol frames with out-of-range values or invalid sequences to trigger undefined behavior in {{targetName}}

T-005.threat: Compromised {{sourceName}} injects tampered data into downstream {{targetName}}
T-005.cause: {{targetName}} trusts data from {{sourceName}} without integrity verification
T-005.attack: Attacker who controls {{sourceName}} manipulates outgoing data causing {{targetName}} to act on falsified information

T-006.threat: Physical cable tampering — data flow manipulated via accessible cable or connector
T-006.cause: Data flow runs through a physically accessible cable without physical protection
T-006.attack: Attacker splices in a tap device or signal injector and manipulates data in transit without triggering any alarm

T-007.threat: Integrity attack on safety-relevant data flow — false values reach safety function
T-007.cause: Safety-critical data flow carries no end-to-end integrity protection
T-007.attack: Attacker modifies values on the safety data flow causing the safety function to operate on false data

T-008.threat: Unauthorized write access via OT protocol — attacker modifies process values or configuration
T-008.cause: OT protocol data flow is configured with read-write access — any node can issue write commands without authorization
T-008.attack: Attacker places a rogue node on the OT network and sends write commands to modify setpoints or controller configuration
